To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a method that allows to identify transposon insertion mutants by massively parallel sequencing of insertion flanking sequences.
we developed a massively parallel method for the identification of insertion element flanked sequences in large populations of insertion mutants.
we developed and tested a highly efficient method to identify dTph 1 transposon insertion mutants by massively parallel sequencing of transposon insertion sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a highly efficient method for massive parallel sequencing of insertion element-flanking sequences from large mutant libraries, which can be easily applied to other insertion element systems and to the generation of large flanking sequence collections.
the development of methods for the efficient identification of insertion mutants in plants and their subsequent functional characterization.
the development of a highly efficient and cost-effective method to generate transposon flanks in a massively parallel fashion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the method described in this paper can be used to generate large flanking sequence libraries in parallel, which will greatly accelerate the process of transposon mutagenesis in plants and other organisms.

the use of the dTph1 flanking sequence database for the identification of insertion mutants is highly recommended and that the described method is an efficient tool for the generation of such a database.
our method provides a fast, efficient, and highly parallel way to create flanking sequence databases for any transposon system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an efficient method to generate large flanking sequence libraries in parallel.
we were able to identify 100% of all insertion mutants in our library by using our method.
we have developed a highly efficient and scalable method for the generation of flanking sequences from insertion element mutants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parallel sequencing of transposon insertion sites is a highly efficient method that is suitable for the identification of insertion mutants from large populations.
the parallel identification of insertion sequences is possible in a single reaction by using the multiplex PCR technique.
it is possible to identify transposon flanks from thousands of individuals in parallel using a single sequencing run, thus allowing to identify transposons in a single day.
